newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Bruised dollar encounters key support.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Bruised dollar encounters key support.

text.p: Dollar/mark should continue to move lower and dollar/yen remains vulnerable but important support near 1.4950/70 marks and 111.00 yen should prevent big losses, at least in the near term, technical analysts said.
"I think the dollar is going down," said Ture Johnson, technical analyst at Bank of America. "With that being said, everything is sitting right around (good) support."
After important support near 1.5000/05 marks eroded early in U.S. trade on Monday, the dollar fell to 1.4965, near a major high on August 22 and major trendline resistance earlier this year.
"We're looking at support at 1.4963 marks, then the Fibonacci level which corresponds with that chart level at 1.4948," said Pete Grant, senior foreign exchange analyst at MMS International.
This area represents a 61.8 percent retracement of the dollar's rise from 1.4635 marks in July to 1.5455 on October 17.
A break below 1.4950 marks could get pretty ugly, analysts said. Minor support near 1.4880 marks notwithstanding, the dollar should move quickly down to the 1.4650 area they said.

Likewise, a close below 111.00 yen may prompt more dollar selling. But analysts are divided over whether dollar/yen's recent slide from the October 29 high at 114.91 is simply a retracement of the dollar's rally this year.
"If it does give way, look for a little bit of downside extension to 110.58 yen," said Grant. "But I still think these losses are corrective in nature."
But if dollar/yen holds below 111.50, Johnson looks for a major decline in the next day or two.
Resistance at 1.5030/50 marks should contain the dollar topside in the short term, analysts said.
At 1200 EST on Monday, dollar/mark was quoted at 1.4975/85 marks, down from 1.5045/50 at Friday's close and at 111.06/11 yen, down from 111.70/75.
